## Observations

1. In year \(i\), only aliens who became adults in earlier years can give a stone. If \(g_i\) of them give, alien \(i\) finishes that year with \(s_i=A_i+g_i\) stones.
2. After year \(i\), alien \(i\) never receives another stone. It therefore gives one stone in each of the next \(d_i=\min(s_i,N-i)\) years, in a single consecutive interval, and finishes with \(B_i=s_i-d_i\).
3. The gift count \(g_i\) is the number of giving intervals that cover year \(i\). Each interval starts after the year in which it is determined, so a difference array can maintain this count in a single left-to-right pass.

## Solution sketch

1. > The gift count \(g_i\) is the number of giving intervals that cover year \(i\). Each interval starts after the year in which it is determined, so a difference array can maintain this count in a single left-to-right pass.

   Initialize a zero-filled difference array indexed through year \(N+1\) and a running gift count of zero. Process the aliens in year order. At the start of year \(i\), add the difference-array entry for that year to the running count. The result is \(g_i\): all intervals covering year \(i\) were scheduled in earlier years.

2. > In year \(i\), only aliens who became adults in earlier years can give a stone. If \(g_i\) of them give, alien \(i\) finishes that year with \(s_i=A_i+g_i\) stones.

   After applying the changes for year \(i\), compute \(s_i\) by adding the running count to \(A_i\). Do not count alien \(i\) as a giver in its own year. In particular, the first alien receives no gifts because no interval has been scheduled yet.

3. > After year \(i\), alien \(i\) never receives another stone. It therefore gives one stone in each of the next \(d_i=\min(s_i,N-i)\) years, in a single consecutive interval, and finishes with \(B_i=s_i-d_i\).

   Compute \(d_i\) and record \(B_i\). If \(d_i>0\), add one to the difference-array entry for year \(i+1\) and subtract one at year \(i+d_i+1\). This counts the alien as a giver through year \(i+d_i\), inclusive. If \(s_i=0\) or \(i=N\), the interval is empty and no update is needed; when \(N=1\), the sole answer is \(A_1\). After the pass, print the recorded answers in order, separated by spaces. Each year requires constant work, so the algorithm uses \(O(N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space.
